text:
Ottawa and Los Angeles both arrive after losses two days ago, and both are thin up front. The Senators fell 4-1 at Vegas and are 2-3-0 in their last five, without Thomas Chabot and William Eklund. The Kings lost 2-1 in Chicago and are without Mats Zuccarello, who had 54 points last year; Joel Armia has taken his spot beside Haula and Laferriere. There's a homecoming too: Warren Foegele, who played 129 games for the Kings, is back in Los Angeles for the first time since leaving.

Neither side has been winning the chance battle. Expected goals measure the quality of shots taken and allowed, and both teams sit near even at five on five (OTT 50%, LAK 48%). Ottawa's power play (0.81 expected goals a game) outranks Los Angeles's (0.54), and the Senators draw more penalties than they take, though they still give up 4.8 a game. Our model has it close, 3.08 expected goals for OTT to 2.79 for LAK. In net, projected starters Samuel Ersson (OTT) and Darcy Kuemper (LAK) are both below expectation this season, at -4.4 and -1.4 goals saved above expected. Last year's marks were -17.8 and -6.8, so neither goalie can steady a shaky team.

Among the players to watch, Tim Stützle gives Ottawa the best odds of any skater (35% to score, 74% to get a point). Drake Batherson, a 121st overall pick in 2017, had a hat trick on Saturday. For Los Angeles, Adrian Kempe has the best goal chance at 35%, with Artemi Panarin close behind at 34% and 71% to pick up a point.
